content.text:
All done — the flight ended on schedule. Here's the recap.

**Ovelaro — New Year 2027 installs campaign (Dec 30, 2026 – Jan 12, 2027, Lagos time)**

Structure: one campaign ("Ovelaro New Year 2027 — Installs", id t6w91), 3 line items, one per approved post, each targeting Nigeria + Ghana + South Africa, iOS and Android only, ALL_ON_TWITTER placements, optimization goal WEBSITE_CONVERSIONS against the "App installed" pixel (dlxut). No new posts were written; no app-install campaign was created.

What happened during the flight:
- Dec 31: all three line items delivering, ~$22–25/day pace, evenly split ($8.33/day each).
- Jan 6: Post C ("cutoff") was trailing on link clicks (33 vs A 52 / B 43) at equal spend, so I paused it and moved its budget into A and B ($12.50/day each). A and B finished essentially tied.
- Line items ran to their end_time (Jan 12, 23:00 UTC = midnight Lagos, end of Jan 12) and stopped serving.

Totals over the full window:
- Spend: **$260.01** of the $350 budget (A $144.23, B $144.21, C $61.57 — C also accrued ~$3.38 of billed charges after the pause, which is normal lag)
- Impressions: **465,593** (A 189,344 / B 190,728 / C 85,521)
- Link clicks: **248** (A 106 / B 107 / C 35) — overall ~0.053% CTR, ~$1.05 per link click

Notes and caveats:
- The $350 was a ceiling; actual delivery came in ~$90 under (pay-by-impression, standard delivery). Unspent budget was not used — I didn't raise budgets mid-flight beyond the A/B rebalance.
- The pixel reports installs as "App installed", but install counts aren't exposed in the stats I can pull, so the recap is spend/impressions/link clicks only; I can't verify install volume from the ads side.
- Financial-services authorization was in place for NG/GH/ZA and all three promoted posts showed approval_status ACCEPTED; nothing was disapproved.
- Post C's poor early CTR is the main reason it was paused; its time-sensitive angle might still be worth retesting in a future flight, since it was only given ~7.5 days of data before rotation.
